analysis.title: Ahold Delhaize NV (AD.AS): First Take: 3Q26 EBIT +4% beat; FY26 guidance reduced due to cyber incident (FCF guide now €2.1bn, from at least €2.3bn)
key_insights: Ahold Delhaize 3Q26 group cFX sales growth was +1.9% on net sales of €23,089mn, against company-compiled consensus of +1.1% and €22,943mn. Europe cFX was +3.1% (consensus +1.8%) and U.S. cFX was +1.1% (consensus +0.6%).

Group LFL sales ex-fuel rose +1.2% against consensus +0.7%. Europe was +2.1% (+2.0% ex-calendar, consensus +1.3%). U.S. was +0.5% against consensus +0.3%, including a -0.6% hit from pharmacy IRA, a -1.5% hit from egg deflation, Cyclospora outbreak and SNAP changes, and a +0.2% calendar benefit.

Group 3Q underlying EBIT was €946mn at a 4.1% margin against consensus €910mn and 4.0%, about 4% above. Europe was €389mn (4.0% margin, consensus €375mn), U.S. was €565mn (4.3% margin, consensus €558mn), and AD Group was -€9mn (consensus -€23mn).
Group diluted underlying EPS was €0.69 against consensus €0.65, about 6.2% above. Underlying net income was €603mn against consensus €573mn.

The cybersecurity incident is expected to reduce 4Q net sales by €200mn to €250mn and underlying/IFRS EBIT by €75mn to €100mn. U.S. pharmacy sales impact is $450mn with non-material impact on adjusted EBIT.

FY26 guidance changed: underlying operating margin approaching 4.0% (from around 4.0%, consensus 4.0%), underlying cFX EPS growth low single digit (from mid-to-high single digit, consensus +1.5% y/y to €2.71), free cash flow around €2.1bn (from at least €2.3bn, consensus €2.26bn), gross capex c.€2.7bn (consensus €2.59bn).
GS says flowing the 3Q beat and the midpoint of the cyber impact through implies about a 1% downgrade to EBIT consensus. The updated FCF guidance is about 7% below consensus.
GS keeps a Neutral rating with a DCF-derived 12-month price target of €39, implying about 13.5x FY27E P/E (13.7x EV/NOPAT). Price was €32.16 at the 3 Nov 2026 close, 21.3% upside to target.

market_movers.rationale: Neutral rating and €39 DCF-based target kept after the 3Q26 EBIT beat. FY26 free cash flow and EPS guidance were cut because of the cyber incident.

earnings_insights: 3Q26 reported 11/4/2026: group underlying EBIT €946mn (4.1% margin) vs company-compiled consensus €910mn (4.0%), a 4.0% beat. Underlying diluted EPS €0.69 vs consensus €0.65, underlying basic EPS €0.69 vs consensus €0.66.
3Q26 reported net sales €23,089mn vs consensus €22,943mn (+0.6%). Group cFX growth +1.9% vs consensus +1.1%. LFL ex-fuel +1.2% vs consensus +0.7%.

3Q26 U.S. reported: net sales $15,267mn vs consensus $15,196mn, underlying operating income €565mn vs consensus €558mn (+1.3%), margin 4.3% vs 4.2%. Europe: net sales €9,822mn vs consensus €9,739mn, underlying operating income €389mn vs consensus €375mn (+3.7%), margin 4.0% vs 3.9%.

FY26 guidance after 3Q26: free cash flow around €2.1bn (prior: at least €2.3bn, consensus €2.26bn). Underlying cFX EPS growth low single digit (prior: mid-to-high single digit, consensus +1.5% y/y to €2.71). Underlying operating margin approaching 4.0%. Gross capex c.€2.7bn vs consensus €2.59bn.

The cyber incident is guided to cut 4Q net sales by €200mn to €250mn and underlying/IFRS EBIT by €75mn to €100mn. GS estimates a c.1% downgrade to EBIT consensus and FCF guidance about 7% below consensus.
risk_factors: Upside risks: acquisition synergies above expectations, weaker EUR vs USD lifting translation, faster U.S. market share gains from price investment, GLP-1 behaviour shifting into higher-margin categories, and faster online grocery profitability.

Downside risks: higher integration costs, inability to pass inflation through to consumers, stronger EUR vs USD, continued U.S. share loss becoming a structural drag, aggressive competitor price investment in Europe, trading down or reduced food-at-home spending from SNAP headwinds or GLP-1 uptake, and a faster shift to online groceries that dilutes margin.
Cyber incident cost in 4Q: net sales down €200mn to €250mn and EBIT down €75mn to €100mn.
